text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Istanbul's Fenerbahce soccer club sees $25 million revenue from life insurance services which it plans to offer its supporters.
- The Tourism Ministry turns down an Islamist demand to change regulations on travel agencies that organise Moslem pilgrimages to Mecca.
- Businessmen, angered by the political situation, call for politicians to make way for successors.
- The right to import second-hand cars free of duty, currently extended to expatriates, will be given to residents of Turkey if they open a 50,000 mark account at a Turkish bank.
- Wanted crime boss Abdullah Catli, who died in a car crash with a top police official, was given his gun licence by the former interior minister who resigned after the crash scandal emerged.
- The government approves lower duty on cars produced in the Far East.
- Parliament passes a law aimed at curbing money laundering.
- Businesmen call for the government to bring to light ties between organised crime and the state.
